name: Camera_ResetWorkEntries

name: maybe_Field_EffectDesc_CreateSpriteMesh

name: maybe_Field_ActorComponent_RefreshVisualA

The new detail is that the gate is the UI overlay mode byte and the flag passed to Field_GetActorAnimSpeedMultiplier is 1 here and 0 in the twin 0x001E0B90, i.e. a resume/pause pair.

name: maybe_Field_ActorComponent_RefreshVisualB

evidence: Same body as 0x001E0990 except the constant 0 instead of 1; still no callers and no vtable slot, so the class stays inferred from the address cluster. The 1/0 pair reads as resume/pause of field actor animation while a UI overlay is open.

name: Field_ActorMove_Begin
signature: void Field_ActorMove_Begin(FieldActorMoveTask* task, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)

name: Field_ActorMove_End
signature: void Field_ActorMove_End(void* task, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: End hook of the field actor move task: sets the global actor animation speed multiplier to 0, resets the target actor's animator and freezes the scene object on the last animation frame.
evidence: Exact mirror of the start hook 0x001E0E20 (same two named callees, flag 0 instead of 1, SetAnimatorLastFrame with 1 instead of 0), so the start/end pairing is now supported by both bodies rather than by the address cluster alone.

name: maybe_Field_ActorMove_Cancel
signature: void maybe_Field_ActorMove_Cancel(void* fieldAction, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)

name: maybe_Field_Actor_PauseAnimation

name: maybe_Field_ClimbAction_PauseAnimation

name: maybe_Ui_PartyPanel_UpdateCounter

name: maybe_Ui_Jackpot_StoreRectPairIfPromptConfirmed
signature: void maybe_Ui_Jackpot_StoreRectPairIfPromptConfirmed(void* widget, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)

name: maybe_Ui_Jackpot_StoreRectPairIfPromptNotConfirmed

summary: Chooses one of two rectangle pairs from the jackpot-screen callback table and stores it at widget+0x50/+0x54: when the prompt at +0x4C is absent or its first choice was not confirmed it enables the UI view and uses pair [0x28]/[0x29], otherwise pair [0]/[1].

name: Event_AdvanceFlagState7To8
signature: void Event_AdvanceFlagState7To8(void* idSet, u32 flagId, int arg3, int context)

What exactly it unlocks is still unknown.

evidence: Same callee set and same ring offsets as 0x001FC95C, so the family is certain; which of the two variants is used where is not, and there are no callers.

name: maybe_Battle_IncrementUnitCounters
summary: Walks the four 0x1C-stride battle unit rings at +0x4298 and, for every live unit (virtual +0x10 non-zero) whose flag byte +0x39D has none of bits 0x46 set, bumps the per-unit counter at saveWork+0x3AE4+id*4 through func_00612A94 (99999 cap).

name: maybe_Menu_MeasureAverageActorWidth_Tail

There is no prologue, the loop branch jumps back into the enclosing function and the body is Ghidra decoding the middle of the measure loop (coprocessor_function plus a run of bogus Gfx_EffectParams_Create calls).

name: maybe_Ui_EquipmentWindow_InitCategoryRows

name: maybe_Gfx_Movie_IsIdEnabled

name: maybe_Field_SceneObject_ClearQuestStateByte
signature: void maybe_Field_SceneObject_ClearQuestStateByte(u32 index, u32 kind, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)

summary: Forwards the event to the child scene nodes, then for event 5 on an idle actor (f_43 clear) whose f_2EC latch is still clear it copies the global player 2D class id into f_2F0 and sets f_2EC.
evidence: The only callee is the named Field_SceneNode_ForwardCommand, so the 'forward then handle one event id' shape is certain; what event 5 means and what the global at 0x007A3F6C is remain unidentified, and there are no callers.

name: Actor_ResetIdleAnimAndTrail
summary: Picks the actor's idle/standby animation (0x1B when f_43 is set, otherwise 4, 5 or 1 depending on the UI overlay byte and the current motion id) and then resets the trail sample record through Gfx_Trail_ResetSamples.
evidence: The named callees Gfx_Trail_ResetSamples and Actor_ResolveReferenceObject plus the explicit animation ids read straight off the body support both halves of the name, and the named caller ModelPreview_UpdateAttachments is consistent with it.

name: maybe_Ui_FrameScript_Update
summary: Generic per-frame step driver: advances the 1/30 s timer and frame counter, dispatches the callback of the current 0x18-byte step record from the table at +0x11C (limit 0x16) through the adjustor table, and rebuilds the shared UI core object when the +0x11DA latch is set.
evidence: The 0x18-byte step-record dispatch is the same template as 0x00304840 and 0x003B4A48, so the shape is certain, but the only caller is maybe_Ui_RecipeBook_Ctor and no vtable slot ties it to a concrete screen, so 'FrameScript' stays a description rather than a class.

name: Ui_MessageWindow_UpdateNextArrow
summary: Timer-driven message-window tick: while the window reports not busy through virtual +0x4C it subtracts the 1/30 s frame delta from the float timer at +0x188 and, when the timer crosses zero, clamps it to -1 and sets the next-indicator text on the child pane at +0x13C.
evidence: The vtable neighbours Ui_MessageWindow_LoadLayout and Ui_MessageWindow_ReleaseBase settle the class, and the countdown-then-set-text pattern is exactly a blinking next-arrow; the arrow wording itself is still an inference from that pattern.

name: maybe_Ui_WindowStateSlot_Step
summary: Advances a window's two-entry state queue: adds the 1/30 s frame delta to the slot timer, bumps the frame counter, then invokes the callback selected by the step index at +0x360 through the 0x18-byte entry and the adjustor table at +0x37C.
evidence: Same 0x18-byte step-record template as 0x00261F40 and 0x003B4A48 (only the slot count, 2 here, and the table offset differ), and the vtable neighbour maybe_Ui_WindowStateSlot_DispatchPending supports the class; no callers.

name: maybe_Ui_MessageCmd_UpdateQueue
summary: Frame update of a message-command window controller: accumulates the 1/30 s delta and frame counter, then dispatches the callback of the active slot (index < 9) from the 0x18-byte entry table at +0xD8C through the adjustor table at +0xDAC.
evidence: Third copy of the same 0x18-byte step-record template (slot limit 9, table at +0xD8C); the owner class is still ambiguous because the vtable 0x00768BEC mixes message-command and three-row text windows, and there are no callers.

name: maybe_ModelPreview_SelectAttachmentSlot
signature: void maybe_ModelPreview_SelectAttachmentSlot(void* preview, const u8* slot, u8 value)

name: maybe_Field_SceneNode_Register

summary: Third copy of the idle-advance step, testing input-manager slot +0x34; when it is empty the child at self+8 is asked to switch to state 3 through its virtual +0x14, and the function always returns 1 so the caller treats the frame as handled.

summary: Per-screen UI slot-handle setup: gets the UI core and calls Ui_SmithMenu_SetAllSlotHandles(core,1,0x0B), then the still-unnamed setter 0x00625FC0(core,1,1,0x0B).

summary: Links the widget into two host intrusive lists (host+0x114 and host+0x98) through the list-link helper 0x001235A4 and stores the two callback descriptors on the widget.
evidence: The two inserts and the descriptor stores are readable, but the body is register-damaged (unaff_r4..r8) and the single caller is the equally uncertain maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_CreateParts, so the 'BindCallbacks' wording stays a description.

name: maybe_Ui_GuideWindow_RefreshPageText
summary: Refreshes the guide window's text window from the current page message id (Ui_GuideWindow_GetPageMessageId -> Ui_GuideWindow_SetTextFromMessage), then copies the two style words from g_uiGuideWindowPageCallbacks.
evidence: The named callees Ui_GuideWindow_GetPageMessageId and Ui_GuideWindow_SetTextFromMessage show the function refreshes the page text; nothing in the body releases a page node, so the old 'ReleasePageNode' name was wrong. No callers.

name: maybe_Ui_GuideWindow_AdvancePage
summary: Advances the guide window to the next page: increments the page index and, when a page list exists, refreshes the rows and re-applies the page value, then copies the two style words from g_uiGuideWindowPageCallbacks.
evidence: The named callees Ui_List_UpdateRowA and Ui_GuideWindow_SetPageValue show a page advance, not a counter increment as the old name said; it is distinct from Ui_GuideWindow_NextPage (0x00369AD4), and there are no callers.

name: maybe_Ui_CompareRow_SetValueFromMemberId
summary: Resolves the party member record for the id at *memberIdPtr (0x0035EB98), computes the clamped difference value through 0x00629280 and stores it on the row via Ui_CompareRow_SetValueA.
evidence: The callee 0x0035EB98 is the documented party-member record accessor, so the byte read is a member id, which the old 'FromByte' wording hid; the named callee Ui_CompareRow_SetValueA confirms the row side.

name: Model_Actor_HideAttachment
summary: Hides an actor attachment by sending state 4 through vtable slot +0x3C and clearing the shown flag at +0x26F.
evidence: Two of the four callers are named and both are attachment-visibility paths (Battle_ActorAction_UpdateMotion, Battle_ActionModel_UpdateAttachmentVisibility), which matches the state-4 call plus flag clear exactly.

name: maybe_Ui_Panel_UpdateStateA
summary: Battle party-panel step A: at timer 0x14 it picks cue 0x3A/0x3B/0x3C from the party count and plays a layout animation, and at timer 0x15 it fills four member rows from the battle party list at ui+0x100 and fires cue 0xE9C.
evidence: The timer-driven body and the named callees Ui_Cue_Start / Ui_Panel_PlayAnimObject are readable, but there are no callers and the sibling step B is also only a maybe_ name, so the panel class is unproven.

name: maybe_Ui_Panel_UpdateStateB
summary: Battle party-panel step B: at timer 10 it fires cue 0xEA4 and plays a layout animation, at timer 0x1E it fills four member rows and fires cue 0xE9C, and from timer 0x33 it enters panel state 0x0B.
evidence: Same timer skeleton as step A with the named callees Ui_PanelState_Enter0B and Ui_Panel_PlayAnimObject; no callers and the family is still only a maybe_ name.

name: maybe_Ui_RecordDetailWindow_BuildRows_Tail
summary: Not a real function: a mid-function split symbol inside Ui_RecordDetailWindow_BuildRows (0x0037C6F8). There is no prologue or epilogue and the decompiled body (unaff_r4 plus virtual calls that are not in the disassembly) does not match the real code.
evidence: The dossier records that 0x0037C8E0 lies inside 0x0037C6F8 with no prologue/epilogue and that the body's calls are absent from the disassembly, so the old 'BuildRowsTail' name described a fragment rather than a function.

name: maybe_Ui_RecordDetailWindow_HandleInputE
summary: Window input handler: pops the sub-pane on event bit 4, forwards the event position to the widget at +0xB4, and on event bit 0x102 pushes one of three sub-panes according to the row-type byte at self->f_EC->f_C, each with its own text index and descriptor pair.
evidence: The three-way sub-pane push and the descriptor table are fully readable and the callees Ui_Window_PopSubPane / Ui_WidgetStack_PushAt are named, but there is no caller and the row-type field's meaning is still inferred.

name: Ui_PaneAnim_ApplyToChildren
signature: void Ui_PaneAnim_ApplyToChildren(void* layout, void* target, u32 frame, u32 flags)
summary: Applies one animation frame to the layout's own anim target (Ui_Layout_ApplyAnimFrame) and then forwards every animatable child pane of the layout's child list to func_0053CD1C, skipping part-pool objects.
evidence: The two named callees Ui_Widget_UpdateAnimatedChildren and Ui_Layout_ApplyAnimFrame fix both halves of the body, and the child walk with the part-pool type test is explicit; only the damaged argument forwarding at func_0053CD1C keeps it at 0.5.

name: maybe_Ui_DiveForm_OnValueStep
summary: Value-step handler of a numeric field: releases the row tweens and then steps/applies the field animation.
evidence: The body is mostly unrecoverable (overlapping Thumb instruction, coprocessor_loadlong, software_interrupt, halt_baddata) and only the first two calls are trustworthy, so both the DiveForm prefix and the step direction are unproven.

name: maybe_Ui_ClearPendingInputA
summary: When Container_RingBuffer_Next reports another queued input event, clears the pending-input word at UiCore+0x94.
evidence: Both callees (Container_RingBuffer_Next, Ui_GetCore) are named and the twin 0x00387058 has the same body, so the action is certain; the owning window is unnamed and the argument in r3 was dropped, so the descriptive A name stays.

name: maybe_Ui_ClearPendingInputB
summary: Copy of 0x00382AD0: when Container_RingBuffer_Next reports another queued input event it clears the pending-input word at UiCore+0x94.
evidence: Identical 52-byte body to 0x00382AD0 with the same two named callees; it is used by a different window, so no single class name can be given.

name: maybe_Ui_Actor_GetPortraitIdB
summary: Second portrait-id query: resolves the character record for id 0 through the data manager, looks up the portrait table entry, maps the 0xFF miss to 0 and writes the byte id, u16 style and size byte to out.
evidence: Six named callers now use it, and they are all overlay/actor-overlap paths (Ui_OverlaySlot_UpdateStateMachine, Ui_Overlay_TestActorRectOverlap, Ui_Window_TestActorOverlapAtSlot), which supports the 'actor display descriptor' reading; the table getter is still a maybe_ name and the layout differs from 0x00386B54.

name: maybe_Field_SceneNode_Reset
summary: Installs vtable 0x00768278, releases the child at +8 and clears +4, then resolves the embedded object at self+0x14 and returns it (result - 0x14); a reset/release, not a getter.
evidence: Fifteen named callers now exist and most are UI icon paths (Ui_QuestIcon_SetScreenPos, Ui_MapIcon_ProvideShipIcon, Ui_MapIcon_BindQuestActor), which does not fit the 'Field_SceneNode' class; the vtable global is itself a maybe_ name, so the class stays open.

name: maybe_Ui_TextWidget_Ctor
summary: Constructor of the message-window text widget: allocates the object, installs g_uiMovieTextWindowVtable, initialises the three intrusive list heads at +0x11C..+0x134, runs Ui_Object_CtorBase on the embedded element and then installs g_uiTwoColumnTextWindowVtable.
evidence: The only caller is the named Ui_MessageWindow_CreateTextWidget and the body installs the movie-text and two-column-text vtables, so the class is a text widget rather than a generic panel as the old name said; the exact subclass is still open.

name: maybe_Data_CollectLinkedRecords
signature: void maybe_Data_CollectLinkedRecords(void* self, const void* record)
summary: Builds a list of at most five related objects for a record: reads the record's id lists, resolves each id through the generation-tagged handle table and stores the object into self+0x10[n], bumping the count at +0x24.
evidence: The generation-handle resolution and the five-entry limit are visible, but the 936-byte body is heavily damaged (Heritage warnings, literal-pool reads) and the only caller (Ui_MessageWindow_SetTextByIdAnimated) does not pin down which relation is collected.

name: maybe_Ui_Marker_RetryBindTarget
summary: Retry counter step: increments the counter at self+8 while it is below 10; the rest of the body is lost to bad instruction data.
evidence: Only the capped counter increment is readable (the rest is coprocessor_movefromRt plus halt_baddata) and there is no dossier, caller or callee list, so neither the marker class nor the 'bind target' role can be verified.

name: maybe_Battle_ActionSequence_BuildMemberRowB
signature: u32 maybe_Battle_ActionSequence_BuildMemberRowB(void* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Damaged Thumb copy of the battle member-row builder: same self+0x2EAB/0x2EC1 slot arithmetic, Text_BuildRowForMember and the paired-slot attach.
evidence: The body is register-starved (unaff_r5/r6/r7, lost arguments) and the only named callee is Text_BuildRowForMember, so the builder reading is plausible but unverified; no callers.

name: maybe_Battle_ActionSequence_BuildMemberRowC
signature: u32 maybe_Battle_ActionSequence_BuildMemberRowC(void* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)

name: maybe_Ui_DiveForm_PopPanesToState
summary: Pops dive-form panes while Ui_DiveForm_PopPane succeeds, stopping at a slot whose +8 state word is 1.
evidence: The body is badly damaged (halt_baddata, coprocessor_load, unaff registers) and only the PopPane loop is recoverable, so both the class and the stop condition stay inferred.

name: maybe_Ui_DiveForm_OnConfirm
signature: void maybe_Ui_DiveForm_OnConfirm(void* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Input handler of the dive form: flag bit 2 pops a pane, the 0x142 mask hit-tests the button and either pushes the detail pane or writes pending result 0xFFFF and pops panes to the handler; bit 0 forwards the stored input triple.
evidence: All four callees are now named (Ui_DiveForm_PopPane, Ui_DiveForm_PushPane, Ui_DiveForm_PopPanesToHandler, Ui_List_IsCursorAtPartyEndRow) and the branch structure is stable, but there are no callers and the handler also contains a generic pop/forward path.

name: maybe_Field_TalkBalloon_Dtor
summary: Deleting destructor of a small object owning one sprite at +0x64 and an embedded Ui_Object: stamps the vtable, destroys the sprite and the Ui_Object body, then frees the instance.
evidence: The teardown shape is certain (Gfx_Sprite_DtorAlt, Ui_Object_DtorBody, 0x0010F6CC) but there is no caller and no data reference that identifies the class, and the same body appears at several addresses.

name: maybe_Field_ObjectSprite_Dtor_D7714
summary: Deleting destructor of a small sprite object: stamps the vtable, destroys the sprite at +0x4C through Gfx_Sprite_DtorAlt, destroys the embedded Ui_Object body and frees the instance.
evidence: Same three-step teardown as 0x003D95F8 with only the sprite displacement changed, so the family is certain; no caller or data-table reference identifies the class, which is why the address suffix stays.

name: maybe_Field_Actor_DeleteSubObjects
summary: Deleting destructor of a large field-actor class: stamps the vtable, destroys two sprites and three Ui_Object bodies reached by folded displacements, then frees the actor.
evidence: The stamp-vtable / nested-teardown / free shape with five members is clear and the callees are named, but the class is a layout inference only (the address appears in no data table) and there are no callers.

name: maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_BuildPartTable
summary: Walks the command's parts and, for each part in animation state 3, writes a 0x18-byte drawable entry plus six sub-part entries with flags 0x10/0x20/1/2/4/8 taken from the part's bytes +0x12..+0x17.
evidence: The named caller Ui_MessagePage_ExecuteCommand and the callees Ui_Part_GetAnimState / Ui_MessageWindow_ClampTextPosition support the role, but the 406-byte body is damaged (unaff_r10/r11, bad instruction data), so the name stays maybe_.

name: maybe_Field_ActorAction_CtorAlt
summary: Constructor of a field-action subclass: allocates through Actor_Action_InitDescriptor and installs g_fieldActorActionAltHandlerVtable, differing from the base only in slot +0x10.
evidence: The vtable it installs is g_fieldActorActionAltHandlerVtable, which names the subclass, and the only caller is the named Actor_CreateActionTable; the overriding slot 0x003E4008 is still unnamed, so the subclass identity cannot be stated.

name: maybe_Gfx_SubObject_InitMeshAndEffect
summary: Loads a mesh by name through Gfx_SceneNode_LoadMeshByName and replaces the effect object with Gfx_EffectObject_Replace using the zero vector.
evidence: Both callees are named and the two-step body is clear, but there are no callers and the owning class is unknown, so the generic Gfx_ prefix is kept.

name: maybe_Gfx_SceneObject_CreateFromDefs
signature: void maybe_Gfx_SceneObject_CreateFromDefs(u32 owner, void* def1, void* def2)
summary: Builds a renderable scene object from two definition blocks: copies a 5-word descriptor from def1 and a 2-word one from def2, calls the shared scene-node constructor 0x002D97E8 and installs a vtable.
evidence: Four of the five callers are named and all build render objects (Gfx_CollisionProxy_InitDesc, Gfx_SpriteObject_CtorWithVectors, Field_ObjectSprite_UpdatePoseRaycast, Field_ModelObj_ReleaseSprite), which supports the reading; the vtable it installs is named g_uiMessageWindowVtableF, which does not fit and is probably a misnamed global.

name: maybe_Field_SceneObject_FinishTalkText
summary: End-of-talk step: writes 0xFF into the shared per-object state byte at work+0x24A98+0x5A4E+slot when the node is idle, and if that byte is 1 or 4 refreshes the talk target through 0x002D1258.
evidence: The named callees Field_SceneObject_Show and Anim_PlayByIdForActor plus the 1/4 state test are readable, but the byte index resolves to the shared quest/pastword block, so whether it is a quest id or a per-object message state is still unclear.

name: maybe_Field_SceneObject_FinishMessageAction
signature: void maybe_Field_SceneObject_FinishMessageAction(void* node, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 ctx)
summary: Variant of the talk-action completion: clears the shared state byte to 0xFF when idle, and when the byte is 1 or 4 plays the talk animation through virtual +0x84, calls 0x005F7784(node,0x3C,0) and clears node[0xAD].
evidence: Same shared state block and the same '1 or 4' test as the sibling 0x0040F680, and it sits next to Field_SceneObject_Hide in table 0x0076DC40; there are no callers, so the exact action name stays a description.

name: maybe_Ui_TextWindow_LoadTextAndEffectClips
signature: void maybe_Ui_TextWindow_LoadTextAndEffectClips(void* window, u32 arg2, void* callback)
summary: Loads and starts the window's two animation clips: the 'txt_1' text clip into window->textClip and the '_effect' clip into window->effectHandle, each through Ui_AnimClip_Load and then its virtual +0x54.
evidence: The two string literals 'txt_1' and '_effect' and the two Ui_AnimClip_Load calls show the function loads both clips, which the old 'LoadEffect' name hid; the body is damaged (unaff_r6, nonsense callback argument) and the only caller is Ui_MonsterBook_InitData.

name: maybe_Ui_TenRowWindow_RebuildRows
summary: Validates the attached actor against the part-pool sentinel list, rebuilds the rows through Ui_TenRowWindow_BuildRows, resets the scroll counter and re-selects the row by id, then clamps the row index to 0..9.
evidence: The named callee Ui_TenRowWindow_BuildRows names the window class the old 'MessageWindow' prefix guessed, and Ui_List_SelectEntryById confirms the re-selection; there are no callers.

name: maybe_AnimObject_OnEvent
signature: void maybe_AnimObject_OnEvent(void* self, int eventId, uintptr_t forwarded)
summary: Event hook: on events 1 and 2 it samples the global pause byte at (work+8)+0x44 into self->isPaused, then forwards the event to the base anim-object handler.
evidence: The callees AnimObject_ForwardEvent and Ui_ResolveObjectHandle name the base class, so the old 'Field_PathMover' prefix had nothing behind it; there are no confident callers, so the event ids stay unexplained.

name: maybe_Ui_TenRowModePanes_Setup
signature: void maybe_Ui_TenRowModePanes_Setup(void* window, void* layout, u8 mode)
summary: Caches ten named row panes plus one extra pane into a window, selecting the descriptor table by the mode byte (2, 3, other).
evidence: Two named callers (Ui_ThreeModePaneWindow_InitPanes, Ui_ModeListWindow_InitPanes) and the fixed 10-iteration loop fit, but the body is damaged (unaff_r6, register-forwarded vtable calls), so the name keeps maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_FourRowTextWindow_Ctor
summary: Tiny constructor: runs the base object constructor, installs g_uiFourRowTextWindowVtable and clears the pointer at +0x4C.
evidence: The vtable it installs is g_uiFourRowTextWindowVtable, which names the class the old address-suffixed 'Widget_Ctor_53A8' left open; the only caller is Ui_SakusenWindow_Ctor, so it is a sub-pane of the tactics window.

name: maybe_Ui_TwoLineMessageWindow_Ctor
summary: Constructor of a two-line message sub-pane: runs the base object constructor, installs g_uiTwoLineMessageWindowVtable and clears the three pointers at +0x50/+0x54/+0x58.
evidence: The vtable it installs is g_uiTwoLineMessageWindowVtable, which names the class; the only caller is Ui_SakusenWindow_Ctor and the paired destructor is 0x00479800, so it is a tactics-window sub-pane.

name: maybe_Text_Row_InitFromRecord
summary: Fetches the data manager and calls the record resolver 0x0063D178; the rest of the body is lost to bad instruction data.
evidence: The decompilation hits halt_baddata right after Game_GetDataManager and func_0063D178, so the record id and the stores are lost; the only caller is Battle_PickWeightedCandidate, which gives no record-type evidence and does not fit the 'Text_Row' prefix.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_UpdateAutoAction
summary: Vtable-slot-4 update of a small field gimmick: runs the base scene-object update and, while enableAutoAct02 is set, slot 0 of the work table at +0x2FB18 is empty and the animator exists, replays the 'Act_02' action name (or the alternate name when work+0x27715 is clear).
evidence: The body reads the gimmick's own enableAutoAct02 flag and the literal action name 'Act_02', which the old address-suffixed 'Gimmick3107' name hid; the callees Field_SceneObject_Show, Data_IsSlotEmpty and Anim_PlayByIdForActor are named, but there are no callers.
